newsitem.title: USA: Dodgers says News Corp. interested in team.
newsitem.headline: Dodgers says News Corp. interested in team.

text.p: The Los Angeles Dodgers baseball team said on Tuesday that it was seeking permission to sell the team to News Corp.'s Fox Sports unit.

"Peter O'Malley, president of the Los Angeles Dodgers, announced that the Dodgers, pursuant to the rules of Major League Baseball, have (Monday) requested permission to enter into serious discussions with the Fox Group, an affiliate of News Corp.," the team said in a statement. The Dodgers, controlled since 1950 by the O'Malley family, said Fox was one of several groups that had expressed interest in the team.
A spokesman for the commissioner said the Major League Baseball Executive Council will consider the request. A News Corp. spokesman declined to comment.
But a source close to News Corp. confirmed the two sides were in talks, adding, "Something should happen in the middle or end of next week."

The Los Angeles Times and Newsday reported on Monday that Fox was interested in buying the Dodgers, one of the premier franchises in sports. The Wall Street Journal, quoting people familiar with the situation, reported Tuesday that News Corp. has agreed to pay about $350 million to buy the team, which played in Brooklyn before moving to Los Angeles for the 1958 season.
O'Malley announced in January that the club was for sale.
